title: R1 minimal experiment: intent-to-binary fidelity of math lowering in ONNX-MLIR (development container)
frozen_at_utc: 2026-09-30T05:37:19Z (file mtime; the value first written here, 05:50Z, was an estimate and is corrected). Written while the compiler variants were being built and before any model compile (first: 05:39:10Z single-op scan), correctness or timing run
basis: MLIR research-item note R1 (scratchpad MLIR_연구아이템_노트_20260930.md), sections 2.3-2.7

arms.r1a: I1 only: patches/r1_i1_math_approx_benefit.patch (legacy approximation op set, PatternBenefit 2 > MathToLLVM 1)
arms.r1b: I1 + I2: plus patches/r1_i2_gelu_pow_to_mul.patch (Gelu x^3 as x*(x*x) instead of math.pow)
arms.identity: each variant is identified by its binary SHA-256 (recorded at build time); the reverted rebuild must equal orig

compile: default flagset: -O3 --march=x86-64 --mcpu=emeraldrapids (+ --opt-report=Simd for full models); every model built with an explicit distinct --tag or loaded alone in its own process

hypotheses_and_predictions.H1_static: orig: the vector Gelu loop calls scalar tanhf and powf once per lane. r1a removes tanhf (and other libm calls of approximated ops) but not powf; r1c removes powf but not tanhf; r1b removes both. Falsified if the calls remain.
hypotheses_and_predictions.H2_detection: the libm call-site count per op in the final .so, compared with the opt-report SIMD claim, identifies every op whose reported vector code calls scalar libm per lane, without timing.
hypotheses_and_predictions.H3_effect: r1b makes the Gelu kernel and the BERT model substantially faster than orig without changing answers (see gates).

metrics.static_primary: libm call sites per symbol (tanhf, powf, expf, erff, logf, sinf, cosf, ...) in each .so; opt-report SIMD lines per op kind
metrics.single_op_numerics: max abs and max relative error vs a float64 numpy reference, and vs ONNX Runtime, on a fixed seeded input set; descriptive (no pass/fail threshold)
metrics.model_numerics: start/end logits max abs difference vs the orig arm and vs the saved ORT@256 reference logits; descriptive
metrics.timing: fresh process per arm (one model per process), block-randomized order, CPU 3, 1 thread; per block log ratio; mean and 95% t-interval over blocks. Development container: NOT a result

gates_fixed_before_measurement.semantic_gate_model: full SQuAD v1.1 dev set (all 12,006 features) at L=256 with the official postprocessing: (a) questions whose predicted answer text differs between r1b and orig <= 10 (0.1% of 10,570), and (b) |EM(r1b)-EM(orig)| <= 0.1 and |F1(r1b)-F1(orig)| <= 0.1 points. Researcher's choice: it tolerates rare argmax flips at near-ties, not a systematic change. Checked once; not tuned afterwards.
gates_fixed_before_measurement.timing_interpretation: a timing effect is interpreted only if |relative effect| >= 10% (about 3-5x the 2-3% block sd of this container) and its 95% interval excludes 0; otherwise reported as not distinguishable here

stop_or_shrink: calls remain after the intervention -> H1 rejected for that op; report as is
semantic gate fails -> accuracy problem of the approximation path; report, do not tune
only Gelu shows the divergence in the single-op scan -> bug report + upstream patch, not a paper
vectorized approximation not faster -> H3 rejected
